 This Crl.P Is Filed U/S 438 Of Cr.Pc Praying To
Grant Anticipatory Bail To The Petitioners / Accused
No.1 And 2 In Cr.No.356/2023 In The Event Of Their
Arrest For The Offence P/U/S 406 And 420 Of Ipc, Which
Is Pending On The File Of Prl. Civil Judge And Jmfc At
Doddaballapura And Said Crime Registered By The
Doddaballapura Rural Police, Bengaluru Rural
District.
 This Petition, Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2 are before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.356/2023 of Doddaballapura Police Station pending on the file of the learned Principal Civil Judge and JMFC at Doddaballapura registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant viz., Sidda Giriyannavar.
Heard Sri.Krishna B.J., learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt.K.P.Yashodha, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioners are entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioners being the accused Nos.1 and 2 are seeking grant of anticipatory bail on the apprehension of being arrested.
It is stated that the Manager of the Criyagen Agri and Biotech Private Limited filed the first information against accused Nos.1 to 3 for the above said offences on 21.10.2023.

entities.text: Criyagen Agri and Biotech Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The offence said to have been committed between 01.12.2021 to 14.06.2023.

sentences.text: It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that petitioner No.1 had filed a complaint against the Directors of the said company on 12.07.2023.
Since, the police have not registered the complaint, the private complaint in PCR No.142/2023 came to be filed.
The learned counsel submits that the learned Magistrate referred the matter for investigation and that is the motive for the registration of the private complaint.

Even though the allegations are of serious nature for having misappropriated huge sum of more than Rs.27 Lakhs, I am of the opinion that the petitioners may be granted anticipatory bail reserving liberty with the Investigating Officer to seek their custody for interrogation in case of necessity, with the permission of the jurisdictional Magistrate.

6. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
The petitioners are ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of their arrest in Crime No.356/2023 of Doddaballapura Police Station.

The petitioners are directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order and on their appearance,
the Investigating Officer shall enlarge them on bail subject to the following conditions:-
a.
The petitioners shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.

e. If in case, the Investigating Officer deems it necessary to subject the petitioners for custodial interrogation, he is at liberty to do so, with prior permission from the jurisdictional magistrate.
On furnishing the sureties by the petitioners, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by them.

On satisfaction of the said documents, he may proceed to accept the sureties within a reasonable time.
